videos.script: Lesson 1 said a lambda takes the type of the place it is written. This lesson is about those types. {{one}} Any interface with exactly one abstract method can be written as a lambda. Java calls it a functional interface, and an annotation makes the compiler check the promise. {{four}} The standard library ships forty-three of them, and four shapes cover almost all of it. A function takes a value and gives one back. A predicate answers yes or no. A supplier gives a value from nothing. A consumer takes one and gives nothing back. {{prims}} Most of the rest are the same four for int, long and double, so that a number never has to be wrapped in an object. {{own}} And then the one case where none of them fits: reading a file. The method can fail, and Function has no room for that. You will write the interface that does.
